title: Dialog Boxes
summary: Dialogs are windows built from a template, with keyboard navigation and default buttons for free. This lesson creates modal and modeless dialogs, writes the dialog procedure, moves data in and out of the controls, validates input, and returns a result.

cards.q: What does a modal dialog do to its owner, and when does `DialogBoxParamW` return?
cards.a:
It disables the owner and runs its own message loop; the call returns when `EndDialog` is called

Returning only when closed is what lets the caller test the result (`IDOK`) on the next line. A dialog that leaves the owner usable is modeless.

cards.q: How does a dialog procedure differ from a window procedure?
cards.a:
It returns `TRUE` or `FALSE` for handled, never calling `DefWindowProcW`

Returning `FALSE` lets the dialog manager do the default. It initialises in `WM_INITDIALOG`, not `WM_CREATE`, and a modal dialog is closed with `EndDialog`.

cards.q: Why should a modeless dialog's messages go through `IsDialogMessageW`?
cards.a:
Otherwise its Tab, Enter, Esc and mnemonic keyboard handling does not work

A modeless dialog uses the main message loop, so that loop must give it the keyboard handling a modal dialog's own loop does. Close it with `DestroyWindow`, not `EndDialog`.
